task_message:
Case V63: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 241x241x89 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is complete. 

**Summary of what I did:**
1. **Located the lesion** with axial, coronal and sagittal contact sheets plus targeted single-slice views. The abnormality is a markedly T2-hyperintense, lobulated/septated soft-tissue mass in the right lateral abdominal wall (distinct from the bright external skin markers at the body edge, the liver parenchyma, and bowel).
2. **Started the mask** with two positive points on the hyperintense lobules (marks 499 and 439) at the axial slice through the lesion's largest cross-section, giving a single connected 22.4 mL component.
3. **Verified in three planes** — zoomed axial, coronal and sagittal crops confirmed the green outline hugs the bright lesion boundary; the extent tapered appropriately at both cranio-caudal ends (small residual sliver at the volume edge).
4. **Rejected all auto-candidates**: C1 (66 mL) and C2 (47 mL) were large crescents of dark surrounding muscle/fat and fascial planes; C3/C4 were tiny unrelated specks.
5. **Final review** showed no lesion tissue in the past-the-mask panels, so the mask was saved.

Confidence: medium — the hyperintense core is clearly delineated in all planes, though the precise extent of the less intense periphery/flow-void region carries some uncertainty.
